title: CC-tier oracle_call updates only the f64 amplitude cache, not the exact map: effect discarded by the next gate
description:
Found 2026-11-01 by read-through (not yet reproduced by a test).

In src/cc.rs, fn apply_invocation, the Invocation::Oracle branch (around line 1259-1298) iterates state.amps (the binary64 cache), XORs payload/code into each basis key, and writes the result back with 'state.amps = next'. It never updates the private QuantumState.exact map in src/action.rs. Every gate (apply_exact), permutation (map_basis) and is_clean check rebuilds self.amps from self.exact via refresh() (src/action.rs ~line 88). Consequence: a CC-level oracle_call followed by any action gate, qexch, qfree cleanliness check or measurement on the same QuantumState silently discards the oracle's XOR into the target and fault registers. The action-tier path exec_oracle_call (src/action.rs ~line 1229) is correct: it uses map_basis and a memo cache.

Also in the same branch: the oracle is re-run once per basis key with no memoisation (the action path memoises by projected inputs), and the branch does not use controls_plus/pred handling consistently with the action path.

Fix: route the CC Oracle invocation through the same code as action.rs exec_oracle_call (a shared fn taking &mut QuantumState, the projection, target, fault, controls), so the exact map is the single source of truth; delete the amps-only rewrite. Expose a helper on QuantumState if needed rather than touching amps directly from cc.rs.

Red test first: a CC fn that does qreg.new 2 wires in superposition via action_call (h on the input), then oracle_call @inc8-style oracle into a target qreg, then an action_call applying x (or a second oracle_call) to the target, then measure with fixed --draws; expected distribution must show the oracle's XOR (compare against the reference interpreter: differential). Add it to tests/differential.rs as well so both engines are covered.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A failing test in tests/ reproducing the discarded XOR on both engines (interpreter and jit), then green. 2) cc.rs no longer writes state.amps directly; exact map is the only mutable amplitude store. 3) Differential test against the reference interpreter for a CC program with oracle_call followed by an action gate agrees. 4) Full gate (scripts/pre-push) green on both engines.

title: Cutting-edge qHiPSTER-style dense amplitude simulator engine: cache-optimal, memory-optimal, multithreaded
description:
Maintainer request 2026-11-01: add a high-performance dense state-vector simulation engine to the VM alongside the exact sparse engine (src/action.rs + src/exact.rs), in the style of Intel-QS / qHiPSTER (Smelyanskiy, Sawaya, Aspuru-Guzik 2016) and its successors (Qulacs, QuEST, qsim, cuStateVec on CPU side).

Scope (north star decision 6, §4.2 'simulator target'): a target-selectable engine for Q actions and oracle branch enumeration on larger wire counts than the exact sparse map can hold, used for rung 4(b) Grover end-to-end at N <= 2^8, rung 7(b) and rung 8(b). The exact engine remains the semantic reference (epsilon = 0 proofs); the dense engine is evidence-labelled with a stated floating-point error bound per certificate (north star §5.1 part 2).

Design requirements:
- State: 2^n complex amplitudes, SoA or interleaved layout chosen by benchmark; binary64 default, binary32 optional; memory exactly one state vector plus O(1) scratch (no copy per gate).
- Gate kernels: 1-qubit and controlled 1-qubit gates applied in place with the qHiPSTER blocking scheme: iterate over the state in cache-sized blocks (L1/L2-aware block size, chosen at runtime from the target qubit index: low-index qubits are 'local' within a block and fused; high-index qubits stride across blocks), so each amplitude is touched once per fused gate group. Gate fusion of consecutive gates on the same low qubits into one pass.
- Multithreading: data-parallel over blocks with std::thread (no external crates unless ratified; the crate is std-only today) with a work-stealing or static partition; NUMA-friendly first-touch allocation; thread count from available_parallelism().
- Permutation gates (x, cx, ccx, mcx, swap, qexch, qxor, memory dispatch) as index remaps without complex arithmetic; diagonal gates (z, s, t, rz, cz) as in-place phase multiplies without the 2x2 pass.
- Branch enumeration for lifted oracles on the dense state: enumerate basis indices with nonzero amplitude (or all 2^k input configurations), run the classical oracle once per distinct projected input with the existing memo cache, then apply the XOR permutation to the target/fault bits as an index remap.
- Measurement: parallel reduction for Born probabilities, in-place collapse and renormalisation; deterministic given --draws, obeying the ISA 0.9 K17 draw order.
- Engine selection via BENNETT_VM_ENGINE (e.g. 'dense') and/or target description capability; every existing action test must pass on the dense engine within a stated tolerance, and the differential test against the exact engine must agree within the bound.
- Benchmarks: a tests/bench or examples/ harness reporting gates/s and bytes/amplitude for 20-30 qubits; record numbers in docs/PROGRESS.md. Literature to read first: qHiPSTER arXiv:1601.07195; Jones et al QuEST 2019; Suzuki et al Qulacs 2021; Haner & Steiger 0.5 petabyte simulation 2017 (for the cache blocking + gate fusion argument).

Non-goals for v1: distributed (MPI) simulation; GPU; tensor networks. Those are follow-up beads.

Plan placement: list this under bennett-vm milestone 6 (performance) in docs/PLAN.md and add one line to bennett/docs/plan/2026-10-29-path-to-north-star.md under executors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New engine module(s) under src/ with the blocking + fusion + multithreaded kernels, std-only. 2) All existing action tests pass on the dense engine within a documented tolerance; a differential test exact-vs-dense over the action corpus agrees. 3) Benchmark harness and recorded numbers for 20, 24, 28 qubits: single-thread and all-thread gates/s, memory = 16 bytes/amplitude (binary64) + O(1). 4) Certificates produced from dense runs carry kind 'numerical' with the error bound, never 'exhaustive'. 5) docs/PLAN.md and the north-star plan updated; gate green.
